text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Dutch proposal for closer military cooperation to be discussed at the European Union's Amsterdam summit next week would not take Finland closer to any alliance, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- State is reforming the national health insurance system of reimbursing patients for perscription drugs, increasing the cost borne by the patient to save costs. @

- Speculation persists over identity of a buyer for oil groups Neste's and Statoil's jointly owned petrochemicals group Borealis; Neste says talks have progressed, but that details of a Finnish television report pointing to Abu Dhabi's ADNOC as the buyer are incorrect.
- A young male bear has been spotted wandering through the woods in the town of Vantaa, just several miles from downtown Helsinki, on Thursday and Wednesday nights.
- City of Helsinki celebrated its 477th anniversary with a variety of free events where participants sweated in a heat wave. @
- Colourful and outspoken Finnish politician, former leader of the Rural Party, Veikko Vennamo, died yesterday at 84.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Residents of the island province of Ahvenanmaa are the most active Finnish investors in shares, a study shows.

- To ensure flexibility in Europe's planned monetary union, (EMU), pay deal negotiations should be separated from agreements on other working conditions, Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers TT says.
- National carrier Finnair's board is expected to decide on a major plane acquisition plan today. @
- Finnish regional telephone operators of the Finnet alliance have taken market share in mobile phone call transfer business from leader Telecom Finland, ministry survey shows.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish life-saving association has chosen today, Friday the 13th, for its nationwide anti-accident day.
- Finnish firemens' union has threatened to start a strike in two weeks to back their demands to restore their retirement age to 55 from 65. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Interior ministry plans to re-register all firearms in Finland in a few years and to tighten up the gun control laws.
DEMARI
- Insane price competition distorts the construction business, sector representatives say.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Finnish companies should have equal chances to those of their rivals in other industrialised countries, Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers TT says while reforming its goals for job markets. @
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
